facts.invariant: Advertised operations are a typed operation-id set with availability, required claims, and redaction disposition; generic_api_request never counts as coverage.
Each semantic invocation has one call id, operation id, safe input digest, and exactly one typed result receipt.
A denied operation yields a typed safe receipt naming the failed boundary; secret values and hidden identifiers are absent.
A mutation receipt carries operation id, idempotency key, outcome, stable code, retryability, and safe current revision when applicable.
Every artifact ref is produced by a typed semantic receipt or registered work product and remains linked to the terminal result by run id.
Interaction and approval targets are immutable revision or decision references carried in a typed target envelope.
A blocked or yielded result names a bounded continuation; wake routing remains a control-plane decision and emits only safe causal identifiers.
A budget or cost stop includes a typed reason, observed limit class, safe usage aggregate, and control-plane decision id.
Source-event and semantic mutation idempotency are distinct; an exact semantic retry reuses its stable operation receipt and records the duplicate link.
The controller binds behavior to negotiated typed capability versions, accepts optional extensions, and rejects unknown required versions fail-closed.
Run, session, turn, item, source-event, governed-target, wake, monitor, decision, and receipt identifiers form an inspectable trace to terminal disposition.
Checkout and release, wake routing, budget enforcement, audit persistence, run persistence and replay, assignment, and monitor management are not runner tool calls.
Cross-company discovery, broad audit access, destructive document lifecycle, and company administration require separately governed contracts; v1 rejects rather than tunnels them.
Every accepted additive correction ships golden replay, duplicate and retry, redaction and denial, optional-extension, and unknown-required-version conformance coverage.
